H6HI02426.name: Brenton Awa
H6HI02426.bio: Hawaii state senator first elected in 2022.

positions.stance: Would cap predatory investor buying, expand down payment assistance, give owner-occupants the same tax benefits as investors, and unlock suitable federal land for local homes.
Supports expanding federally funded community health centers across Hawaii and requiring health providers to post prices so patients know costs in advance.
Would require military personnel stationed in Hawaii to pay the standard registration fee, using the added revenue to reduce registration fees for Hawaii residents.
Would pass tariff revenue back to consumers by reducing the federal gas tax and providing incentives for states that lower their own fuel taxes.
Supports increasing the child tax credit and expanding existing federal childcare assistance so more families receive direct help with childcare costs.

H6NH01420.name: Anthony DiLorenzo
H6NH01420.bio: Entrepreneur and community leader in New Hampshire.

positions.stance: "Reduce costs, increase wages, and improve quality of life."
Supports a Balanced Budget Amendment to the U.S. Constitution to balance the federal budget.
Would protect the 2017 tax cuts and the elimination of taxes on tips, overtime, and Social Security.
"Fully support Social Security and Medicare for our citizens."
Promote "policies that bring clarity and common-sense practices to digital asset markets."

H6NH01321.name: Stefany Shaheen
H6NH01321.bio: Entrepreneur and medical research advocate who served on the Portsmouth City Council and Police Commission.

positions.stance: Supports Medicare for All and a public option; would break up health care monopolies, curb drug prices, and expand Medicare to dental, vision, and hearing.
Says Trump's tariffs are illegal and will fight for small businesses, not just large corporations, to get tariff refunds.
Would end Wall Street tax breaks for buying homes, expand support for first-time buyers, cut red tape, and use surplus public land for housing.
Says ICE "must be completely overhauled," including body cameras, banning masks, stopping warrantless searches, and ending raids in schools, churches and hospitals.
Would overturn Citizens United, ban stock trading by members of Congress and senior officials, and impose a lifetime lobbying ban on former top officials.

H4NH02399.name: Maggie Goodlander
H4NH02399.bio: Former Navy Reserve intelligence officer, Justice Department deputy assistant attorney general, and White House senior advisor.

positions.stance: Supports building more housing, making child care and health care affordable, lowering prescription, grocery and utility costs, and ending costly trade wars.
Leading legislation to ban stock trading by senior officials; wants to end corporate PAC money, overturn Citizens United, and set congressional and court term limits.
Supports "Social Security and Medicare you can count on after a lifetime of work."
Says veterans should get the care and benefits they earned and first responders' families should be cared for.
Would protect the freedoms to vote, to make reproductive health care decisions, and to live without discrimination.

H2NH02260.name: Lily Tang Williams
H2NH02260.bio: Entrepreneur who manages rental properties and works part-time as an expert witness on China-related cases; former assistant law professor in Shanghai.

positions.stance: Would cosponsor the U.S. Term Limits Amendment limiting House members to three terms and senators to two.
Would require every bill in Congress to address a single subject, ending massive omnibus bills.
Would mandate on-time, full-year budgets to end funding by continuing resolutions and shutdown threats.
Would prohibit members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from trading individual stocks while in office.
Supports a constitutional amendment requiring the federal government to balance its budget.

H8ME01120.name: Chellie Pingree
H8ME01120.bio: Organic farmer and small business owner, former Maine state senator, elected to Congress in 2008.

positions.stance: Fighting to lower prescription drug costs.
Fighting to protect reproductive freedom.
Fighting to strengthen Social Security and Medicare.
Wants to tackle climate change with clean energy jobs.
Wants to ensure working families can earn a livable wage.

H4ME01160.name: Ronald Russell
H4ME01160.bio: West Point graduate and 30-year Army veteran (Airborne Ranger, Green Beret) who co-founded a small defense contracting business.

positions.stance: Wants violent criminals to serve their sentences and law enforcement and first responders paid a decent wage and given needed resources.
Supports getting "back to the basics" in core subjects, giving parents a stronger voice, measuring results, and reforms like school choice.
Says Congress must restore civility, prioritize bipartisan problem-solving, and end party-line legislation that is quickly reversed.
Supports securing the border, reforming the "amnesty system" with better screening, and welcoming properly vetted legal immigrants.
Would make the Big Beautiful Bill tax relief permanent, add inflation adjustments for lower brackets, and strengthen work-linked credits like the EITC.

H6ME02171.name: Matthew Dunlap
H6ME02171.bio: Maine State Auditor; former executive director of the Sportsman's Alliance of Maine.

positions.stance: "In Congress, I'll fight for universal childcare, good-paying jobs, and a surge in affordable housing."
Will champion protecting Medicare, Social Security, and Medicaid and work to expand coverage so more people have care they need.
"I am 100% pro-labor"; supports the PRO Act, fair wages, safe working conditions, and the right to organize.
Says the decision to terminate a pregnancy belongs to the woman, and safe access to reproductive care should be a constitutional right.

H6ME02148.name: Paul LePage
H6ME02148.bio: Businessman, former mayor, and former Governor of Maine.

positions.stance: Will work to eliminate wasteful spending, which he says drove up inflation, to lower costs for families and seniors.
"Paul will fight to finish the wall, end illegal immigration, and restore law and order."
"Lower taxes. Less red tape. More jobs for Maine families."
Will defend Second Amendment rights, fight government overreach, and stand up for parents and families.
"Paul has always protected, and will always protect, Social Security and Medicare."

H6MT01152.name: Aaron Flint
H6MT01152.bio: Decorated combat veteran and Montana radio host.

positions.stance: Would give Border Patrol and ICE more resources, deport illegal immigrants starting with violent offenders, and oppose sanctuary policies.
Would ban Wall Street from buying single-family homes and make tax breaks on tips, overtime, and Social Security permanent.
Would expand timber harvests and resource extraction, invest in trades training, and cut regulations on small businesses, farms, and ranches.
Supports the Public Lands in Public Hands Act to prevent large-scale sale or transfer of federal lands, and expanded public access.
Supports "No budget, no pay," no pay during shutdowns, a balanced budget amendment, and a ban on congressional stock trading.

H6MT01137.name: Sam Forstag
H6MT01137.bio: Former Forest Service smokejumper and union leader.

positions.stance: Supports large-scale federal affordable housing investment, zoning reform incentives, banning hedge fund home purchases, and restoring the first-time homebuyer credit.
Would give everyone the choice to join Medicare, free for working people, expand it to dental, vision and hearing, and negotiate all drug prices.
Supports universal free childcare, universal pre-K, higher teacher pay, more Pell Grant funding, and keeping public dollars in public schools.
Would fully staff public lands agencies, expand forest management and wildfire mitigation, support responsible timber harvest, and legalize corner crossing.
Would repeal tax cuts for the ultra-rich, raise the corporate rate to 35%, set a millionaire minimum tax, and enact a 5% billionaire tax.

H4MT02098.name: Troy Downing
H4MT02098.bio: U.S. Representative for Montana's 2nd District; former Montana State Auditor, Air Force/Air National Guard combat veteran, and businessman.

H6MT02150.name: Brian Miller
H6MT02150.bio: Helena attorney who has practiced general civil litigation in Montana state and federal courts for nearly 15 years.

positions.stance: Opposes spending more on war in the Middle East, wants troops brought home, and would cut wasteful military spending.
Opposes expanding executive power beyond its bounds; would work to reestablish the authority of the Legislative branch.
Would treat tribes as equal sovereigns, support policies and funding respecting their independence, and prioritize missing and murdered Indigenous women.
Would make Social Security solvency a top priority, partly by undoing tax effects of the One Big Beautiful Bill and reforming immigration.
Supports universal health care through federal funding with state flexibility, plus a national program to relieve medical debt.

H4RI01265.name: Gabe Amo
H4RI01265.bio: U.S. Representative for Rhode Island's 1st District since 2023; former deputy director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs.

H6RI01153.name: Kellie Keenan
H6RI01153.bio: Public health professional and small business owner.

positions.stance: Would lower everyday costs, provide tax relief for working families and seniors, and make housing more affordable and accessible.
Would lower energy costs, increase ratepayer transparency, diversify the energy mix, and explore next-generation nuclear.
Would cut red tape, support small businesses and entrepreneurs, and expand workforce training tied to real opportunities.
Would eliminate wasteful spending, crack down on fraud and misuse of taxpayer dollars, and increase transparency.
Would support marine trades and fishing, expand ocean-based jobs, and protect the coastline while encouraging responsible growth.

H2RI02184.name: Seth Magaziner
H2RI02184.bio: U.S. Representative from Rhode Island since 2022; former Rhode Island General Treasurer and public school teacher.

positions.stance: Fighting to protect Social Security and Medicare.
Fighting to cut costs for working people.
Fighting to make prescription drugs more affordable.
Fighting to protect and expand the Affordable Care Act.
Fighting to enact common-sense gun safety legislation.

H6RI02318.name: Victor Mellor
H6RI02318.bio: U.S. Marine Corps veteran and entrepreneur who built a concrete business in Rhode Island.

positions.stance: Would help first-time homebuyers and streamline permitting to cut costs and speed construction of homes for all income levels.
Would work with the administration to secure federal investment for ports and manufacturers and bring back high-paying manufacturing and trades jobs.
Would push aggressively for domestic energy production to lower fuel costs and reduce inflation.
Says parents, not government or Big Pharma, hold the primary right to decide how their children are educated, raised, and medically treated.
Opposes broad gun bans including on so-called "assault weapons," and would work to block "Red Flag" laws.

H4DE00045.name: Sarah McBride
H4DE00045.bio: U.S. Representative for Delaware's at-large district; former Delaware state senator.

positions.stance: Supports universal, affordable childcare, guaranteed paid family and medical leave, and support for family caregivers and home-based care.
Wants more renewable energy investment, affordable green technology, and a unionized clean energy workforce to reach net-zero emissions as soon as possible.
Will push to end mass incarceration, legalize marijuana and expunge convictions, and prioritize reentry and recidivism prevention.
Will fight to protect family farms and farmland, support the poultry industry, lower input costs, and invest in new farmers.
Will support public schools and educators, ensure students with disabilities have needed resources, and champion workforce development.

H6DE01121.name: Joseph Arminio
H6DE01121.bio: Political scientist (MIT Ph.D.) whose career has been in public policy and teaching.

positions.stance: Champions his "American Prosperity Plan" to restore high growth, get individuals out of debt, and greatly reduce federal debt.
Opposed attacking Iran, supports steering Israel toward the Two-State Solution, and champions what he calls "The Grand Bargain" in the Middle East.
Supports teaching critical thinking and unfiltered economic history, including mandating formal debate for grades 9-12.
Pledges to take the oath seriously and "uphold the Second Amendment and every other provision, without exception."
Agrees with ending sanctuary cities and enforcing the law, saying enforcement funding depends on a thriving economy.

H6SD01141.name: Nicole Gronli
H6SD01141.bio: Small business owner and former South Dakota Rural Development Director.

positions.stance: Would reduce housing, child care, health care, and energy cost pressures, help wages grow, and expand workforce training and apprenticeships.
Would support voting accommodations, quality care and respite support, and laws making life more equitable for people with disabilities.
Would protect Medicare and Medicaid, restore Marketplace tax credits, and make the Rural Health Transformation Fund permanent.
Would fully fund IDEA, protect Title I, support teacher pay, and opposes closing the U.S. Department of Education.
Would protect landowners from eminent domain abuse, strengthen the Packers and Stockyards Act, and remove tariffs on critical farm inputs.

H6SD01109.name: Marty Jackley
H6SD01109.bio: South Dakota Attorney General and former U.S. Attorney.

positions.stance: Will back police, sheriffs, and prosecutors with tools and respect; "Public safety comes first."
"Secure the border, finish the wall, and let law enforcement do its job."
Will fight for fair markets, honest trade, and less Washington red tape for farmers and ranchers.
"The right to keep and bear arms is not negotiable"; will defend the Second Amendment every time.
Supports President Trump's agenda: "Secure the border, cut taxes, and put America first."

H4ND00061.name: Julie Fedorchak
H4ND00061.bio: Former North Dakota Public Service Commissioner, communications business owner, and state director for Sen. John Hoeven.

positions.stance: "Secure our Border."
"Unleash America's Energy and Agriculture Industries."
"Curb Inflation That Is Crushing Families."
"Stop out of Control Spending and Balance the Budget."
"Rein in Overreaching Federal Agencies."

H6ND01049.name: Trygve Hammer
H6ND01049.bio: Marine veteran, former oilfield rig worker, and former 7-12 grade science teacher.

positions.stance: Says people should not be forced to choose between their health and paying rent or buying food.
"Everyone deserves to be treated with dignity and respect"; says Congress must conduct oversight to preserve public trust.
"Profitable corporations and the ultra wealthy need to be paying their fair share."
Opposes raising the retirement age; "I will put the seniors of North Dakota first and protect their benefits."
Supports public schools in small towns and wants Congress to assert its authority over tariffs and restore agricultural markets.

H2AK01083.name: Nick Begich III
H2AK01083.bio: U.S. Representative for Alaska elected in 2024; businessman and former Ford Motor Company employee.

positions.stance: Wants to lower costs by addressing energy, transportation, infrastructure, taxes, and federal red tape; cites no taxes on tips and overtime.
Wants to advance Alaska North Slope gas production, "end the regulatory chokehold," and build high-paying resource jobs.
Fighting for major investments in ports, airports, roads, rail, and the Marine Highway System to connect communities and lower costs.
Supports energy, LNG, mining, timber, and fisheries growth, and faster federal permitting through the SPEED Act.
Co-sponsored the HALT Fentanyl Act and supports securing the border to stop the flow of fentanyl into Alaska.

H6DC01111.name: Denise Rosado
H6DC01111.bio: Lawyer, former federal attorney advisor, and longtime public servant.

positions.stance: Would advocate to roll back and freeze property taxes, especially for seniors, and convert derelict buildings and lots into housing.
Says D.C.'s estate tax exemption must be raised so families can inherit homes and stay in D.C.
Says D.C. residents should not pay federal income taxes because the District lacks a vote in Congress; opposes D.C. statehood.
Supports continued coordination with federal law enforcement and accurate, transparent crime reporting.
"End automated photo-enforcement tickets," which she says push residents who can least afford it into debt.

H6DC01079.name: Robert White
H6DC01079.bio: At-large member of the D.C. Council; former legislative counsel to Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton.

positions.stance: Would confront federal attacks on D.C., protect residents from ICE and unaccountable federal agents, and defend the local budget and home rule.
Will fight for affordable housing, accessible health care, excellent schools, reliable childcare, lower household costs, and good-paying jobs.
Will mobilize Washingtonians and build a national coalition to secure full representation, self-government, and D.C. statehood.
Would launch a "D.C. Forward Economic Plan" securing federal resources for housing, workforce development, and jobs for residents without college degrees.
Would partner with local and federal officials to address crime and invest in youth programs that prevent violence.

H2VT01076.name: Becca Balint
H2VT01076.bio: U.S. Representative for Vermont; former Vermont Senate Majority Leader and middle school teacher.

positions.stance: Introduced the Community Housing Act, investing over $500 billion in affordable housing, renter protections, down payment assistance, and new construction.
"Mental health care is health care"; supports federal action to make mental health care more accessible.
Cosponsors the Freedom to Vote Act and John Lewis Voting Rights Act; supports Supreme Court term limits, stricter ethics rules, and court expansion.
Original cosponsor of the Green New Deal to create green jobs and transition to a clean energy economy.
Supports expanded background checks, Extreme Risk laws, gun violence research, and reinstating the assault weapons ban.

H6VT01085.name: Gerald Malloy
H6VT01085.bio: West Point graduate and retired Army officer who served 22 years on active duty.

positions.stance: Would bring high-paying jobs to Vermont, cut unnecessary federal regulations, support dairy, agriculture and manufacturing, and push fiscal discipline.
Opposes tax increases, supports balanced budgets, protecting Social Security and Medicare without benefit cuts, and patent reform to lower drug prices.
Supports an all-of-the-above energy strategy and renewables innovation "without costly mandates" to lower heating, fuel, and electricity costs.
Would empower parents and local school boards, support school choice and accountability, and reduce student loan burdens responsibly.
Would fully support law enforcement, strengthen border and national security, and hold foreign actors accountable for the opioid crisis.

H6WY00217.name: Chuck Gray
H6WY00217.bio: Wyoming Secretary of State; former six-year member of the Wyoming House of Representatives.

positions.stance: Would protect coal, oil, gas, and energy jobs, stop wind project subsidies, and oppose the ESG agenda.
Supports lower taxes for working families, reducing government waste, and fighting inflation.
Supports voter ID, proof of citizenship to register to vote, and transparent election processes.
Supports President Trump's approach: secure the border, stop illegal immigration, and enforce existing immigration laws.
Would defend the Second Amendment, support pro-life policies, and stop taxpayer-funded abortion policies.
